2025 and 2026 both carry an appended Draft Marking Scheme with official answers, used for Q1(ix)/Q1(xiv) of 2025 and Q1(ix)/Q8(ii) of 2026); all 10 real past board Exam Papers (2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2025 Improve, 2026, 2026 Improve -- the file named 'Question Paper - 2025.pdf' in the exam-papers folder was independently re-confirmed (17 pages, 0 extractable text, identical title page reading 'SPECIMEN QUESTION PAPER') to be a duplicate of the 2025 Specimen paper and its content is cited only once, as a Specimen source, not as a real exam; none of the genuine exam papers carry an answer key in-repo, so their sourced questions are answered from subject knowledge and marked model); and mandatory web research (knowledgeboat.com and icsehelp.com for verified official Selina answers, including exact cranial-capacity ranges cross-checked against a second independent site; oswal.io and icseboards.com for supplementary practice questions not already covered by any repository source, tagged Website). Per the current build process, no diagram images were cropped or embedded in this pass -- every image-bearing question carries an image_placeholder description instead, written from the question's own printed wording and well-established textbook human-evolution content, without opening any image file. A previous, now-abandoned attempt at this chapter left 3 cropped images in assets/Biology/Human Evolution/ -- these were not referenced, opened, or touched in this build, consistent with the no-image-work rule.

Q12. The following questions are Assertion-Reason based questions. Choose the answer based on the codes given below.
(1) A is True and R is False (2) A is False and R is True (3) Both A and R are True (4) Both A and R are False
Assertion (A): Lamarck's theory of inheritance of acquired characters is mainly based on "survival of the fittest".
Reason (R): Lamarck has explained his principle of 'use and disuse' with the example of Giraffe's neck.
(a) (1) (b) (2) (c) (3) (d) (4)

[1 mark(s)] Source: Book — Selina Concise Biology X, Review Questions A.12

Q13. The following questions are Assertion-Reason based questions. Choose the answer based on the codes given below.
(1) A is True and R is False (2) A is False and R is True (3) Both A and R are True (4) Both A and R are False
Assertion (A): The analogous organ to the vermiform appendix in herbivorous mammals is quite helpful in digesting cellulose. But it is considered a vestigial organ in humans.
Reason (R): Vermiform appendix is a wide worm-like tubular structure, projecting from the blind part of the colon (a part of large intestine). Its function is the same as that of the colon, i.e. absorption of water and some remnants of digested food.
(a) (1) (b) (2) (c) (3) (d) (4)

[1 mark(s)] Source: Book — Selina Concise Biology X, Review Questions A.13

Q14. The following questions are Assertion-Reason based questions. Choose the answer based on the codes given below.
(1) A is True and R is False (2) A is False and R is True (3) Both A and R are True (4) Both A and R are False
Assertion (A): The theory of natural selection, proposed by Charles Darwin, is a fundamental mechanism driving human evolution.
Reason (R): Natural selection operates through the preservation of favourable variations that enhance an organism's ability to survive and reproduce, leading to the gradual adaptation of populations to their environments over time.
(a) (1) (b) (2) (c) (3) (d) (4)

[1 mark(s)] Source: Book — Selina Concise Biology X, Review Questions A.14
